clue.text: Footwear: lose it and fall flat

parts.note: to lose it is to lose one's temper, to flip
something that falls flat is a flop, it fails

explanation.surface: A warning that the wrong shoes will make you lose your footing and land flat on your face.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip-flops are light open sandals held on by a thong between the toes.

clue.text: Sloth feeding duck to monkey

indicators.note: one piece feeding another goes inside it, so the duck's letter goes into the monkey

parts.note: a langur is a long-tailed Asian monkey
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A zookeeper's note about a sloth being given a duck to feed to a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth in its sense of idleness or lethargy is a synonym of listless languor.

clue.text: Don't make the village green celebrate

definitions.meaning: a joke reading: rather than colouring the settlement green, colour the whole place crimson
to go out and have a wild, boisterous night of festivity

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out on a riotous spree of merrymaking.

clue.text: Opposite sides hiding a woman's secret drink

indicators.note: the outer letters are hiding the secret, which sits within them

parts.note: left and right, L and R, are opposite sides
an old joke that a woman keeps her age secret

explanation.surface: Two people on opposite sides conceal a woman's private tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a kind of light beer, a common drink.

clue.text: P-petrol so earnestly requested

parts.note: the stutter supplies an extra letter P before the word
leaded is a kind of petrol containing lead

explanation.surface: Someone stammering over the word petrol while begging for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'P-' gives a separate P before LEADED, the old kind of petrol with lead added.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to beg or ask earnestly, so pleaded is requested earnestly.

clue.text: Name like Maria?

definitions.meaning: to name something like something is to call it as such
Maria ... was the celebrated Greek-American opera soprano

explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was the famous soprano, so her surname fits the question mark's hint at an example.

clue.text: Play card game, king second, earning moves

parts.note: loo is an old card game
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to second a motion is to back it

indicators.note: the letters of earning are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A card player plays a game with a king as their second card, and their earnings shift about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges EARNING into IN ANGER. LOOK BACK IN ANGER is John Osborne's 1956 play.
explanation.definitionFit: Look Back in Anger is a famous 1956 stage play by John Osborne.

clue.text: Lack self-restraint having lost money

indicators.note: one word having lost another means that word is taken out of it

parts.note: abstinence is self-restraint from indulgence
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone without self-control goes bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes TIN from ABSTINENCE, leaving ABSENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An absence of something is a lack or want of it.

clue.text: Soldier confronting single adversary?

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of worker ant
the Roman numeral for one, I

explanation.surface: A lone soldier facing a single enemy in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Used as a noun, an anti is someone opposed to something.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is an opponent, someone set against a cause.

clue.text: Warm environment where bird shelters crazy hen on ecstasy

indicators.note: the bird shelters other letters, holding them inside itself

parts.note: a grouse is a game bird

indicators.note: in an across clue the hen comes on after the ecstasy

parts.note: E is the drug-slang abbreviation for ecstasy

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of hen are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grouse protects a drugged-up hen that has gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles the hen into ENH; the bird's name looks like the definition, but the warm environment is the glasshouse built around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse is a glass building kept warm for growing plants.

clue.text: First of defeats causing friction, a bad one?

indicators.note: first of says to take only the opening letter of defeats

parts.note: rubbing is the action causing friction

explanation.surface: A question of whether a loss that begins a run of defeats and causes friction is a heavy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for a defeat from earlier in the clue, so 'a bad one' is a heavy beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A drubbing is a thorough beating, a heavy defeat in a contest.

clue.text: Model caressed him in front of staff — a wind-up?

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: a crew is a staff of workers

explanation.surface: A model caressing a man in front of the office staff, perhaps as a practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reshapes CARESSED HIM into ARCHIMEDES. The device is a screw turned to raise water, hence a wind-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes' screw lifts water by turning a helix inside a tube, literally winding it up.

clue.text: West Midlands town university restricted by county backing unresponsive candidates

indicators.note: the university is restricted by the county letters, held inside them
backing means the county's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Notts is the abbreviation for Nottinghamshire, an English county
cold means unresponsive, unfriendly
the field is all the candidates in a contest

explanation.surface: A university hemmed in by a county that backs only lifeless election candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NOTTS into STTON, and U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton Coldfield is a large town in the West Midlands, near Birmingham.

clue.text: Get to the bottom of a N E French barman?

parts.note: un is the French for a
a joke: Ravel the composer wrote bars of music

explanation.surface: A question about investigating a bartender from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Ravel was a French composer; composers write in bars, hence 'barman'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a mystery is to solve it, to get to its heart.

clue.text: Old French battle won't end, with English yet to arrive

indicators.note: the battle's name won't have its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Verdun was the great 1916 battle in France

explanation.surface: An old French battle drags on with English reinforcements still awaited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't end' drops the N from VERDUN, leaving VERDU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue is late, not yet come when it was expected.

clue.text: One fastens bit of hair on head

parts.note: a lock is a tress, a bit of hair
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A hair clip that holds a strand on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A locknut is a nut that secures another nut, holding a bolt fast.

clue.text: Drink needing bit of head, with style knocked back

parts.note: the brow is part of the head, the forehead

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for style is read backwards

parts.note: elan is flair, style

explanation.surface: A drink that brings a frown, knocked back in style.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown ale is a dark, sweetish kind of beer.

clue.text: Sound home for fish

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for home is said aloud to give a similar-sounding word

parts.note: one's place is one's home

explanation.surface: A healthy dwelling for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish common in British waters.

clue.text: Cryptically opt for grape variety?

parts.note: the letter P sits inside the pair O and T in this word

explanation.surface: A suggestion to choose a grape type in a cryptic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptically' tells you to read 'opt' as wordplay: P is in OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of wine grapes, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Stretch to excess, something to do during our retreat

indicators.note: one word placed during another sits within it

parts.note: a verb is a doing word
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Overwork during our holiday away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something to do' is grammar talk: a doing word. 'Stretch to excess' is the definition, a verb meaning to overload.
explanation.definitionFit: To overburden is to load with too much, stretching beyond capacity.

clue.text: Somewhat unfeeling, unkind, unpleasant matter

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a callous, cruel and nasty affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunk is slang for sticky, messy or nasty stuff.

clue.text: Winter transport carrying plant round lake

indicators.note: the plant goes round the lake's letter, enclosing it

parts.note: sedge is a grassy waterside plant
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A sleigh hauling a plant around a frozen lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a vehicle on runners for travelling over snow.

clue.text: The whole of eternity in torment

indicators.note: in torment says the letters writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: Being tortured for all eternity.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety of something is all of it, every part.
